claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names and dates of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 5 years old. We live together here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. To properly assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more detail.

**Are you the parent or guardian of Alex, and do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and I have full parental responsibility for him. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Are you currently residing in the UK, and have you been a UK resident for the past two years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I've been here for more than two years.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. That's useful to know.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status/indefinite leave to remain in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, or if he's not in education yet, is he under the age at which children typically start school in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 5, so he's just started primary school. He goes to the local primary school full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are there any circumstances where Alex is not living with you - for example, is he in the care of someone else for any period of time, or does he spend significant time elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he lives with me full-time. He's not in anyone else's care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

**Have you claimed Child Benefit for Alex before, or is this your first time applying?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is my first time applying for it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

**What is your current employment status, and approximately what is your annual income (or your household income if you have a partner)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I work full-time and earn around £35,000 a year. I don't have a partner, so it's just my income.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

**Are there any other children you're claiming for, or is Alex the only child you're enquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is my only child, so I'm just enquiring about him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your circumstances:
- You are Alex's parent with full parental responsibility
- Alex is 5 years old and lives with you full-time
- You are a British citizen residing in the UK for more than two years
- Alex is in full-time primary school education
- This is your first application
- Your annual income is £35,000

Based on the UK Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you meet all the requirements for Child Benefit. Your income is below the higher income threshold where Child Benefit is withdrawn, and all other conditions are satisfied.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- You have parental responsibility for Alex
- Alex is under 16 years old and living with you full-time
- You're a British citizen with over two years' UK residency
- Your income doesn't exceed the withdrawal threshold

You can now proceed to apply for Child Benefit through the official channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
